system-boundary-review.ruling: Retain the complete conflict-relevant responsibility/decision state for the current exact boundary draft scope in the same authoritative decision boundary as its review and approval. Do not turn current assignments into independent unconstrained aggregate streams. Narrow accumulated past-scope/version histories and external waiver behavior; a physical draft/publication split is a conditional future design, not the present audit verdict.
system-boundary-review.why: The collection protects an actual atomic rule over its members: one member cannot hold overlapping work and review/approval responsibilities for the same exact version/revision without an accepted exact waiver, and a later backdated assignment cannot invalidate a prior unwaived review/approval decision. This falls under rule4. Record identity alone does not justify separating assignments.

reviews.name: RiskDraft
reviews.scopeDecision: Reverse unconditional merge. Retain a narrow per-risk definition/identifier claim owner; require a named additional invariant before combining it with assessment/governance.
reviews.currentAtomicInvariant: Within tenant/program, a normalized risk identifier has one stable stream identity and one immutable initial creation intent; revisions require the current narrative revision.
reviews.currentIndependence: Risk assessments read only draft existence/program. They receive no narrative revision, content hash, or narrative text. No observed assessment-validity rule is atomically coupled to narrative changes.
reviews.whatBreaksIfSeparated: The identifier claim and original creation intent cannot move to a separate eventually consistent index: two creates could claim the same normalized identity. Narrative versus assessment already resides in separate streams without any implemented freshness coupling.
rationale: The identifier-derived business key and create-intent conflict are genuine owner decisions, even though the class retains little content. State volume alone does not establish that another owner must absorb it.

Merging into the current RiskGovernanceLedger is specifically unsafe as a recommendation: that ledger owns every program risk and has a dictionary of risks, so it would expand the shared revision/boundary.

A future narrow per-risk owner could absorb narrative if the product names an atomic rule such as invalidating a current assessment on narrative revision. Such a new rule is not present in the reviewed source and must not be invented by the audit.
reviews.safestChange: Keep normalized identity and initial create proof together. Fix Revise command identity, exact retry before stale-revision rejection, and changed-intent conflict. Reclassify as a versioned definition state holder only if the identifier claim is deliberately owned elsewhere with equivalent atomic authority.

preservationPlan.reservation: No split required for recommended scope. If moving identity authority, reserve the normalized tenant/program identifier before creating the risk owner, with the same stable creation identity.
preservationPlan.releaseAndRecovery: A failed transfer must leave the original claim authoritative or explicitly release an unconsumed reservation; a recovery process completes interrupted transfers. Never use a projected risk-directory uniqueness check.
preservationPlan.growth: Current retained state is constant; lifetime narrative replay still grows. Establish replay/snapshot policy for this homogeneous lifecycle rather than merging unrelated governance or adding a lifetime revision cap.

reviews.confidence: high for rejecting the proposed unconditional merge; medium for whether the product eventually chooses a definition state holder or broader per-risk owner

reviews.name: WorkDigestPreference
reviews.scopeDecision: Reject an unspecified merge, especially a merge into Member. Keep the narrow consent write authority while deciding whether event-sourced settings are warranted.
reviews.currentAtomicInvariant: A member has one current email digest choice and a valid scheduling zone; a consent-only change preserves the existing zone. This is a small settings authority; no additional cross-field business invariant beyond a current authorized setting was found.
reviews.currentIndependence: The recipient resolver separately admits current active membership, notification opt-out, and verified address. Notification consent changes do not alter membership identity/security state, and membership changes do not decide notification preference.
reviews.whatBreaksIfSeparated: Moving historical preference display to a projection breaks no write invariant. Merging preferences with Member would not establish an observed domain invariant; it would introduce shared physical revisions between consent and identity/security. A replacement settings store must still serialize concurrent consent intent.
rationale: Do not overstate validation or last-write-wins as a rich aggregate invariant. Rule1 makes a versioned settings owner a legitimate simplification candidate.
The supplied merge disposition lacks a concrete owning rule or target. Same member identity alone is exactly the entity-name argument prohibited by rule2.

The immediate correctness fault is logical request identity: an older retried enable can overwrite a later opt-out because only current-value equality is checked. Changing storage boundary without fixing that does not solve consent ordering.
reviews.safestChange: Preserve the dedicated per-member consent authority and add stable mutation identity plus expected revision. If the product elects a versioned settings record instead of an aggregate, retain durable accepted consent facts/attribution where needed and preserve those semantics; no new aggregate or Member merge is implied.

preservationPlan.reservation: No cross-owner reservation is needed merely to change a setting. Delivery admission must consume a current consent value proof according to its owner contract.
preservationPlan.releaseAndRecovery: For a storage transfer, preserve source revision and accepted command identity; switch one writer only after exact state/proof transfer. Do not replay an old enable as new intent.
preservationPlan.growth: Retained state is constant. All toggles still replay for member lifetime; evaluate event-sourcing cost explicitly. Do not add a maximum toggle count or couple consent to unrelated membership writes.

reviews.confidence: high for rejecting merge into Member; medium for retain versus a versioned settings-store replacement

reviews.name: AdvisorHandoff
reviews.scopeDecision: Retain compact handoff selection/access/admission authority; separate each feedback thread lifecycle. Do not create an aggregate for each historical correction or response merely because it is historical.
reviews.currentAtomicInvariant: Initial feedback is admitted only when handoff is ready and open and its exact source version is selected. Corrections/responses/resolution refer to an existing feedback contribution and preserve the original contribution.
reviews.currentIndependence: After admission, CorrectFeedback, RespondToFeedback and ResolveFeedback do not consult handoff status or selection. Two feedback threads have no cross-thread write rule. Current/historical disposition is computed for reading from selected source references.
reviews.whatBreaksIfSeparated: Checking a projected handoff status or obtaining a stale selection snapshot before creating feedback would admit feedback after revocation. Moving only ReadFeedback history out while retaining every feedback write in handoff would leave lifetime replay and physical revision contention in place.
rationale: There is a real reason to retain the initial admission gate in the handoff; the source comment correctly identifies that race. That does not justify every later correction/response in the same stream.
Feedback identity and correction identity already exist, and subsequent behavior is keyed by feedback, not by the set of all feedback.

History views should remain projections. A feedback thread can retain its current contribution/correction/resolution state and selected command proof without retaining every prior response as owner state unless another rule requires it.
reviews.safestChange: Use a feedbackId-keyed feedback owner for contributed content and its behavior; keep exact-source initial admission versus revocation in handoff. Keep original accepted contribution facts, and project rosters/history.

preservationPlan.reservation: Handoff first decides an admission with stable feedback/command id and exact selected source plus selection epoch; a pending admission is an owner obligation, not merely a live read. Once admitted, later revocation must not silently erase that accepted obligation.
preservationPlan.order: For one handoff, reserve handoff admission before feedback creation. If a command ever needs multiple source owners, sort tenant/owner/identity canonically and record the sequence.
preservationPlan.releaseAndRecovery: A recovery reactor completes feedback creation from the admitted intent or explicitly cancels/releases an unconsumed admission. Consume once with changed-intent conflict; never discard an unknown downstream creation.
preservationPlan.growth: Keep only pending admissions/current access state in memory and no all-feedback roster. Admission events still grow with accepted feedback: this is the actual shared invariant and requires a replay strategy; corrections/responses no longer extend that stream.

reviews.name: AuditPackage
reviews.scopeDecision: Target independent build execution and recipient delivery/disclosure lifecycles. Retain a coherent publication authorization owner for exact current manifest, selected archive, validation and complete override rule. Historical versions/attempt lists belong in projections or immutable content storage, not one new aggregate per list element.
reviews.currentAtomicInvariant: Delivery must target the current exact manifest with a successful archive, a current passed or fully overridden validation, and an exact-recipient disclosure approval. A validator cannot approve their own override; all blocking findings must be overridden before authorization. Delivered content is intended to be immutable.
reviews.currentIndependence: Build attempts have stable attempt ids and monotonic progress; recipient/purpose approvals and recipient/provider-reference deliveries have their own identities. Progress of one build and delivery to one recipient need not stale another recipient action. A validation plus its finding overrides is a real cross-member authorization rule and should remain coherent.
reviews.whatBreaksIfSeparated: Reading latest validation/disclosure projections before a delivery would allow an amendment/new validation to race authorization. Splitting every finding/override independently without a complete-override commit would lose the all-blocking-findings rule. Parent history removal alone does not isolate build progress/delivery physical revisions.
rationale: The broad split verdict is supported, but its implementation must distinguish true independent lifecycles from immutable history.
Current caps on build/validation/approval/delivery history are evidence of the wrong retained state; removing caps without redesign is insufficient.
A compact per-publication-version authorization owner can keep current validation and overrides together; do not introduce separate roots for each validation history entry by default.
reviews.safestChange: Keep manifest identity, current publication status, selected successful archive proof, current validation plus overrides and delivery admission coherent. Put worker progress/retry state in a process record. Give recipient disclosure/delivery stable ownership where their own decisions require it. Store old immutable manifest/version content by digest and project history.

preservationPlan.reservation: Delivery first reserves a publication authorization for exact package/version/manifest hash, chosen archive hash, validation revision and recipient approval. Seal or fence that content selection so later amendment/validation cannot silently change an already accepted delivery intent.
preservationPlan.order: Acquire publication/version authorization before any external delivery. If recipient approval has a separate mutable owner, use canonical owner-key ordering and persist the acquisition sequence.
preservationPlan.releaseAndRecovery: On known pre-send failure release unconsumed authorization; on unknown provider effect reconcile the stable provider/delivery key before retry or release. A recovery reactor completes or terminates pending deliveries and consumes authorizations exactly once.
preservationPlan.growth: Current authority retains unresolved obligations/current facts, not all builds/deliveries/versions. Its admission replay still needs justification; independent worker progress and recipient history no longer grow its revision. No invented maximum delivery count.

reviews.confidence: high for targeted split; medium for exact number of new domain roots until recipient approval/revocation contract is specified

reviews.name: AuditorRequest
reviews.scopeDecision: Retain request terms/open state and an exact response admission/closure coordinator. Split response behavior and independent comments/sample selections; project histories. Do not turn every response version/review/history entry into an aggregate.
reviews.currentAtomicInvariant: Resolution requires at least one admitted response and an accepted immutable external disposition for every admitted response. A response must deliver its exact submitted/approved version, with independent review when required, and delivered versions cannot be revised.
reviews.currentIndependence: Response draft/revision/review/delivery/disposition is a lifecycle keyed by responseId. Comments have their own identity but no effect on response validity. Sample selections have stable identity and exact frozen population provenance. None requires retaining every other response body or comment.
reviews.whatBreaksIfSeparated: A projected response count/accepted count would race concurrent response admission and allow premature resolution. Separately checking open state before a response action also loses the source-owner admission rule. Response-local review/author separation and exact delivered-version immutability must travel together.
rationale: The all-responses-accepted rule is strong evidence against naive child splitting. It justifies a compact set of unresolved admitted response obligations, not all response contents/history.
Accepted disposition is immutable, so an accepted obligation can be discharged once and need not remain a permanent child roster. Stable command proofs are still needed to prevent double discharge.
Comments and sample-selection history should not make a response review stale; the current physical stream does so regardless of logical child version.
reviews.safestChange: A response owner keeps current version, author/review, delivery and immutable disposition with exact command semantics. Request owner serializes open-state admissions and resolution against outstanding obligations. A comment may be an immutable contributed fact under stable identity; it needs no multi-event history owner unless edits/replies add behavior.

preservationPlan.reservation: Reserve request admission before creating a response or accepting a response mutation governed by open request state. While resolution seals admissions, it must see at least one admitted response, no unresolved reservations and no outstanding unaccepted response obligations.
preservationPlan.order: Acquire request admission before response mutation. For multiple request/response reservations, use canonical stream key order with a durable sequence.
preservationPlan.releaseAndRecovery: A recovery reactor materializes reserved responses or explicitly cancels unconsumed creations. Accepted exact-version disposition discharges its obligation once; failed/unknown operations remain pending until reconciled. Reopen begins an explicit new admission epoch while preserving prior immutable dispositions.
preservationPlan.growth: Outstanding obligations may grow while unresolved and are justified by the actual completeness rule; do not hide this with a maximum response count. Completed bodies/history are projected. Admission replay remains part of this request lifecycle and needs an explicit replay strategy.

Response revision is local-versioned; delivered versions immutable.
Independent reviewer decision belongs to exact response version.

reviews.name: AuditPopulation
reviews.scopeDecision: Narrow the real cross-row reconciliation authority and split independent exports. Do not recommend splitting mutable rows into independent aggregates without an exact freeze protocol, or treating every frozen historical version as a new behavioral aggregate.
reviews.currentAtomicInvariant: A reconciliation must exactly account for all current rows in every classification and the complete latest source boundary; freeze binds that exact definition/source/rows/reconciliation digest and keeps incomplete results sample-ineligible. Changing any row or adding source facts invalidates current reconciliation.
reviews.currentIndependence: Exports from an already frozen immutable version have stable export identity and cannot change any row or reconciliation. Frozen prior payloads and amendment history are immutable content/read history, not evidence that every historical version requires aggregate behavior. Row classifications, however, are direct inputs to the current cross-member rule.
reviews.whatBreaksIfSeparated: Independent row updates after a projected reconciliation read can produce a frozen population whose category/source totals no longer match its content. Rule4 expressly permits a collection when such a rule is atomic. Splitting every row on rule3 alone would destroy the actual invariant.
rationale: The current design is oversized and retains/serializes prior versions/exports, but a legitimate cross-member atomic rule exists; size is not proof that all members are independent.
The smallest safe scope is retain current reconciliation authority, remove immutable-history copies from owner state, and isolate export lifecycle.

If current population size cannot fit the transport/storage constraints, immutable content chunks plus an exact sealed manifest/revision proof are a storage design; chunks need not become independent domain aggregates. The owner must still atomically decide completeness.
reviews.safestChange: Keep a current population revision/digest, classification accounting and source completeness authority. Store immutable source/row/version content outside repeated event bodies using exact content-addressed references with existence/integrity proof. Project all version/export history. Separate export authorization/result behavior keyed by export identity where needed.

preservationPlan.reservation: If mutable rows remain in one decision owner, no row reservation is required. If later partitioning mutable row/classification ownership, first seal source admission and reserve/fence each participating row/chunk revision; reconciliation must consume the sealed exact manifest, never a projected count.
preservationPlan.order: For a distributed freeze, acquire participating source/row revision holds in canonical identity order and persist the complete acquisition plan before sealing.
preservationPlan.releaseAndRecovery: A recovery reactor either commits a frozen version using every held exact revision or releases all unconsumed holds after a known abort. No row may change under a consumed freeze proof; amendments create a successor and preserve predecessor bytes/hash. Failed immutable-content writes must be reconciled before publishing their references.
preservationPlan.exports: An export consumes an exact frozen-version digest proof; no parent export roster/revision is required because frozen content cannot change. Unknown external export/storage effects must be reconciled by stable export id.
preservationPlan.growth: Current row/accounting size is legitimately related to the reconciliation invariant and still requires a real storage/replay design. Do not impose new business row/lifetime limits. Historical payloads and export attempts must not be recopied through every fact.

reviews.name: AuditObservation
reviews.scopeDecision: Retain the observation current-source decision boundary. Do not infer independent response/link lifecycles from event names or command ids.
reviews.currentAtomicInvariant: Corrections preserve exact examination/snapshot lineage and replace only the current received source version; a new response or finding link must identify that current exact source version. Each selected logical command has immutable intent and is checked for retry before OCC.
reviews.currentIndependence: The implementation retains latest response and link, not a child roster/history. Response and link use request identities for accepted facts; no separately-lived response or link lifecycle with its own mutable rules was found. AuditObservation is one source-constrained contribution lifecycle.
reviews.whatBreaksIfSeparated: A concurrent correction can make a response/link target a no-longer-current source version between a value read and child append. Preserving the present rule would require a source-owner admission protocol; no benefit or independent lifecycle was established sufficient to justify that additional protocol.
rationale: The shared revision protects a named current-source rule, so its coupling is intentional.
History retained in the event stream is not itself a prohibited parent history collection. Replay still needs sizing justification, but no lifetime cap or all-history current state is present here.
The selected receipt is an existing accepted business fact held for exact retry, not an emitted technical acknowledgement event.
reviews.safestChange: Keep current source/latest response/link and command-selected accepted fact. Keep historical views as projections. Require authorized source/recording handler before exposing public mutations; current class accepts values and does not read other aggregates.

preservationPlan.reservation: No new split or reservations recommended. If product later defines independently editable responses, preserve current-source admission with an explicit observation-issued authorization or deliberately change the business rule to allow immutable historical-source responses.
preservationPlan.releaseAndRecovery: Any such future authorization requires consume/release/recovery; a projection check is insufficient.
preservationPlan.growth: Only homogeneous observation corrections/responses/links extend this stream; retained current state is constant. Evaluate lifetime replay without inventing a maximum fact count.

reviews.name: ComplianceProgram
reviews.scopeDecision: Remove historical criteria-selection collection from command state while preserving authoritative as-of selection proofs. Keep coherent program date plan together. A separate current criteria-selection owner is a possible targeted split, not yet a required new aggregate.
reviews.currentAtomicInvariant: A program plan orders readiness, Type I date and Type II start/end coherently. Program creation has immutable initial intent. Selecting a current criteria edition does not consult name/plan and is not coupled by an observed cross-field rule.
reviews.currentIndependence: Criteria history exists for as-of source reads and is consumed by readiness/baseline contributors. The date plan is one coherent value object. Independent edition selection has different callers, but source proves only separate current choice, not an independent mutable approval/lifecycle requiring another aggregate.
reviews.whatBreaksIfSeparated: Splitting individual plan dates would lose chronological validation. Dropping criteria history without replacing authoritative temporal lookup would lose exact baseline/readiness source semantics. A stale projection cannot substitute for the contributor current-source check. Splitting current edition from program plan causes no observed write-rule loss, but also needs no invented new business lifecycle.
rationale: Historical selections do not participate in a program command decision and should not be retained as command state.

The existing as-of callers are source contributors, so simply replacing the list with an eventually consistent display projection would weaken correctness. Preserve an authoritative event-history reader or immutable selected-version proof with an explicit source fence.

Shared revision between plan and edition is a contention smell, not sufficient proof by itself that a new aggregate with no stronger invariant is necessary. Narrow current state first; then choose a separate selection owner only with explicit identity/retry/revision semantics and a demonstrated write contract.
reviews.safestChange: Keep creation intent and coherent plan validation. Move temporal selection reads to a dedicated authoritative history/proof reader; retain only current edition/current revision where command decisions need them. If separating current edition writes, use a stable program-scoped selection owner rather than a new aggregate per selection history entry.

preservationPlan.reservation: No new cross-owner reservation is required for independent plan edits and edition choice. Source snapshot/admission paths must use exact historical selection revision/digest plus their existing or strengthened fence; do not use a projection eligibility check.
preservationPlan.releaseAndRecovery: For any owner transfer, keep one writer, transfer exact revision and original intent proof, and recover an interrupted transfer without accepting two independent current selections.
preservationPlan.growth: Removing retained history reduces command state, not physical replay of the existing stream. Event-history lookup/snapshot strategy still needs design; do not claim replay became bounded merely by removing the list.

reviews.confidence: high for narrowing history; medium for whether current edition should eventually receive its own narrow write owner

adversarialDesignReview.name: AdvisorHandoff
adversarialDesignReview.scopeDecision: Retain compact handoff selection/access/admission authority; separate each feedback thread lifecycle. Do not create an aggregate for each historical correction or response merely because it is historical.
adversarialDesignReview.currentAtomicInvariant: Initial feedback is admitted only when handoff is ready and open and its exact source version is selected. Corrections/responses/resolution refer to an existing feedback contribution and preserve the original contribution.
adversarialDesignReview.currentIndependence: After admission, CorrectFeedback, RespondToFeedback and ResolveFeedback do not consult handoff status or selection. Two feedback threads have no cross-thread write rule. Current/historical disposition is computed for reading from selected source references.
adversarialDesignReview.whatBreaksIfSeparated: Checking a projected handoff status or obtaining a stale selection snapshot before creating feedback would admit feedback after revocation. Moving only ReadFeedback history out while retaining every feedback write in handoff would leave lifetime replay and physical revision contention in place.
rationale: There is a real reason to retain the initial admission gate in the handoff; the source comment correctly identifies that race. That does not justify every later correction/response in the same stream.
Feedback identity and correction identity already exist, and subsequent behavior is keyed by feedback, not by the set of all feedback.

History views should remain projections. A feedback thread can retain its current contribution/correction/resolution state and selected command proof without retaining every prior response as owner state unless another rule requires it.
adversarialDesignReview.safestChange: Use a feedbackId-keyed feedback owner for contributed content and its behavior; keep exact-source initial admission versus revocation in handoff. Keep original accepted contribution facts, and project rosters/history.
